per_stock_analysis.AMD: Replay lost 9.8 on 28 fills. The 5s replay markout was −4.75 ticks and the latest live EWMA was −5.23 ticks. The public +0.43-tick continuation after large moves does not justify buying or selling through the spread.
per_stock_analysis.AVGO: Lost 12.3 on 22 replay fills. The 1s markout was already −5.82 ticks, versus −5.64 at 5s. Test entry selection rather than waiting longer for the existing breaker.
per_stock_analysis.CRWV: 148 replay fills produced 0.0 PnL. The latest live EWMA was +0.71 ticks, but replay 5s markout was −0.03 ticks. This is a promising place to test better passive queue selection, not evidence to increase size.
per_stock_analysis.MU: Lost 7.9 on 10 replay fills; 1s and 5s markouts were −7.90 and −8.00 ticks. Its public mean-reversion estimate was only 0.59 ticks over 38 events, and its imbalance signal did not pass the stability check.
per_stock_analysis.NBIS: 150 replay fills lost just 0.6. Live 5s EWMA was +0.65 ticks, but stable 1s imbalance predicted only +0.008 in price, −0.106 net of crossing. Seek passive round trips and measure realized exit prices.
per_stock_analysis.NVDA: Largest replay loss: 14.0 on 16 fills, with −8.84 ticks at 1s and −8.75 at 5s. Live EWMA was also poor at −7.16 ticks. Its apparent lead over SNDK is a separate hypothesis, not a reason to fund NVDA entries.
per_stock_analysis.SNDK: Lost 4.6 on 22 replay fills despite a slightly positive latest live EWMA (+0.15 ticks). The NVDA-to-SNDK move of +3.95 ticks came from 31 events; it is not an executable, independently validated round-trip return.
per_stock_analysis.VRT: Lost 7.7 on only eight replay fills. The 1s markout was −9.62 ticks, near the default ten-tick stop distance. Stable book imbalance predicted just +0.10 tick at 1s, far too little to offset that fill selection.

diagnosis: Live PnL fell 43.9 and ended flat. Replay also ended flat in every stock but lost 56.9, with losses in both halves (37.3 and 19.6). CRWV and NBIS accounted for 298 of 404 replay fills and only 0.6 of the loss; the other 106 fills lost 56.3. The immediate problem is which fills we get, not insufficient turnover or stranded end inventory. In the five largest losing names, the average 1s markout was already within 1.2 ticks of the 5s markout. Stop submissions show that some trades required aggressive exits, but they do not identify the entry route or prove the stops caused the loss. One testable mechanism is visible in execution.py: a flat quote that is not one tick ahead of a protecting wall can still receive a one-lot probe, even behind the external touch. Such a quote can miss routine two-way trading yet fill when the market moves through it. The supplied aggregates do not separate those probes from wall-backed fills. Muster found no stable signal that paid the spread, so there is no evidence for compensating with more aggressive entries.
strategy_plan: Test one change: replace the unprotected one-lot fallback with a one-lot quote at an external touch where other participants have recently traded on both sides. Require a one- or two-tick spread, unchanged bid and ask across polls, and a sell at that bid plus a buy at that ask within the last three seconds. Discard the first batch after a price change because the prints may belong to the previous book. Join only if the reservation price favors that side of mid and joining costs at most one tick relative to the raw plan. This tests whether we can collect passive spread from ordinary flow instead of waiting for a sweep; observed prints are evidence of activity, never hypothetical fills of our new order. Preserve wall-backed sizing, reducing quotes, stops, upstream volume limits and downstream evidence screens. The candidate is unverified: before promotion run python3 -m unittest tests/test_bot.py, the added touch-flow tests, and python3 bot/backtest.py /home/workspace/data/autoloop_28_073055/snapshots/cycle_003 --strategy runner:BacktestBot against the −56.9 Champion. Reject a disconnect, a limit breach, or an improvement obtained solely by going idle. Compare completed round-trip PnL, fills and stop volume by stock on the same chunk and then on untouched data; do not scale until the retained activity earns positive realized PnL.
insights: AMD, AVGO, MU, NVDA and VRT lost 51.7 on just 84 replay fills. In each, average 1s and 5s markouts differed by less than 1.2 ticks: much of the adverse price difference was present before the 5s breaker could observe it.

A displayed exit queue and a recently traded exit price answer different questions. Test them separately: a sell at the unchanged bid and a buy at the unchanged ask evidence two-way activity, but neither proves a newly placed order would have cleared its queue.

import unittest
from types import SimpleNamespace as NS

from bot.touch_flow import TouchFlow


class TouchFlowTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.flow = TouchFlow()

    def poll(self, t, prints=(), b=10.0, a=10.1, own=False):
        book = NS(bids=[NS(price=b)], asks=[NS(price=a)])
        return self.flow.observe(t, {'X': book}, {'X': prints}, {'X': [1] if own else []}, 'team')

    def trade(self, side, px, buyer='other'):
        return NS(aggressor_side=side, price=px, volume=2, buyer=buyer, seller='external')

    def test_requires_recent_both_sides_on_same_touch(self):
        sell, buy = self.trade('ask', 10.0), self.trade('bid', 10.1)
        self.assertFalse(self.poll(0, [buy, sell]))
        self.assertFalse(self.poll(0.25, [sell]))
        self.assertFalse(self.poll(0.5, [self.trade('ask', 10.1), self.trade('bid', 10.1, 'team')]))
        self.assertEqual({'X'}, self.poll(1, [buy]))
        self.assertFalse(self.poll(3.5, [buy]))

    def test_change_or_own_fill_invalidates_evidence(self):
        prints = [self.trade('ask', 10.0), self.trade('bid', 10.1)]
        self.poll(0)
        self.assertEqual({'X'}, self.poll(0.25, prints))
        self.assertFalse(self.poll(0.5, prints, own=True))
        self.assertFalse(self.poll(0.75))
        self.assertEqual({'X'}, self.poll(1, prints))
        self.assertFalse(self.poll(1.25, [self.trade('ask', 9.9), prints[1]], b=9.9))
        self.assertFalse(self.poll(1.5, [prints[1]], b=9.9))
